bar_contract_complete_row.evidence: kn1-20260923/sizing-r2/payloads.json (2,000 real final OKX DOGE 1m bars)
bar_contract_complete_row.superseded: the R1 546 B identity-stripped row relied on a per-product header copied from one row; not lossless across schema/source/provider transitions (Astra R2)

market_cache.process: separate Redis process and config from the control/quota/admission Redis (KD10)
market_cache.image: same redis image digest as stable_redis
market_cache.bar_row_encoding: contract-complete and lossless: the canonical EventEnvelope protobuf without only the LPK-derived fields (instrument uid, venue, market, bar interval), behind a 48-byte state trailer (source offset u64, materializer epoch u64, canonical content SHA-256). Those four are restored from the product's LPK, which is the cache key, so no header is stored; every other field (schema name/version, provider, source id/role, native symbol, instrument id/revision, values, revision, final, supersedes, times, sequences, quality, provenance) stays in the row. A row whose uid/venue/market/interval differ from its key is refused; decode is verified against the stored hash. Mixed-history test: schema, source, provider, role, symbol and instrument transitions plus a correction decode byte-exact with one key.
market_cache.bar_layout: per-product hash buckets of 116 opens in listpack encoding; open time in integer milliseconds. The bucket size is a sizing parameter: bucket bytes land in allocator size classes, so bytes/row moved between 707 and 854 across the measured sizes for the same rows

measured_bytes_per_bar_row.evidence: kn1-20260923/sizing-r2/redis-buckets.json and redis-listpack2048.json (Redis 7.2.14, stable_redis image digest; 2,000 real final OKX DOGE 1m bars; max row 694 B); sizing-f5/redis-listpack512.json for the 512 result
measured_bytes_per_bar_row.with_hash_max_listpack_value_512: every contract-complete encoding converts to hashtable; 512 is not a valid setting for this row

sizing.retained_opens_cap_rule: demanded rows + 2064 headroom per product (10,000 -> 12,064; VN 500 -> 2,564)

other_structures_bytes.evidence: kn1-20260923/sizing-f5/redis-keys.json (MEMORY USAGE of one string key per value size, LPK-length key)
other_structures_bytes.latest_rule: 67 demanded latest products (TRADE 11, QUOTE 10, MARK_INDEX_PRICE 10, BOOK_SNAPSHOT 18, BOOK_DELTA 18) at the largest observed canonical size + 48 B trailer; book 56,495 B bounds both book feeds
other_structures_bytes.header_rule: none: the LPK-derived fields come from the key itself (R2); the R1 per-product header is withdrawn

sizing.staging_rebuild: per-product generation swap: a product is rebuilt into staging keys and published on its own, counted with the product's old generation until its keys are physically reclaimed, so the peak is steady plus two largest products (12,064 rows each: one staging, one old awaiting reclaim). A full staging generation beside the ready one would need about 2,400 MB, above maxmemory; that alternative needs an owner-approved RAM increase and is not taken by default.
sizing.rebuild_concurrency: one product in staging at a time, and the next product starts only after the previous old generation is reclaimed; each additional concurrent product adds up to 2 x largest_product_bytes. A reader pinned to a swapped product detects the change and retries within its bound (contract section 5)
sizing.fit_sensitivity: fits only with the LPK row at an allocator-aligned bucket: at 64 opens (769.4 B/row) the cap is 1,305 MB and the full canonical row's best (769.5) also exceeds maxmemory. Headroom is 5.6 %. KN-3 sets each product's bucket size from its measured row size and re-measures every product before promotion
sizing.status: starting cap for KN-3: re-measured with the real projector and all feeds before promotion; per-product staging is frozen in contract section 5; if the real projector does not fit, typed memory pressure stops promotion - the limit is never raised silently (a RAM increase is an owner decision)

native_stream_profiles.decision: Astra KN-2 R2, 2026-09-24: owner permits measured RAM increases after optimization; no runtime cap is changed by this file

measured_kn2.status: isolated captured-provider fanout evidence, not production capacity

capacity_candidate.status: approved planning envelope, unmeasured at this concurrency; apply only in the relevant bounded phase packet

native_stream_profiles.rule: Do not shrink target consumer demand to fit 256 MiB. Measure after reuse/optimization, reclaim superseded roles only after safe cutover, and report peak old-plus-new footprint. 320 MiB is an arithmetic fit with only 13 MiB headroom, not a capacity certificate. Decode factor eight is empirical, not a universal heap bound.

retention.bar_retained_opens_served: the demanded rows of each product (10,000 for alpha crypto, 500 VN, 1,000 TS 1m inside the 10,000)
retention.bar_revision_audit: append-only revision facts kept for every open inside the retained window; below the durable retention floor a tombstone is published
retention.rebuild_horizon: a cache generation offline longer than the tombstone lifetime rebuilds from a fresh generation; it never overlays a cache that may have missed deletes

state_topics.approval: topic creation and ACLs are a separate KN-3 runtime packet

retention.demand_only: only products with manifest demand are materialized; provider wrappers keep serving bounded on-demand history outside the cache
